items.name: Alteryx

items.why: Horizontal analytics platform - owner example of scope_review. Founded 1997 as SRC LLC, renamed Alteryx 2010; taken private by Clearlake/Insight 2024.

items.name: Strategy
items.description: Business intelligence, reporting, and analytics software sold to enterprises, government agencies, and universities
items.why: Formerly MicroStrategy; renamed Strategy in 2025. Horizontal BI product, same shape as the Alteryx example. Note the public company is now primarily a bitcoin treasury vehicle alongside the software business - strategy.com foregrounds MSTR bitcoin metrics.

items.name: RF-SMART
items.description: Barcode inventory and warehouse management software extending Oracle NetSuite and Microsoft Dynamics ERP for distribution, manufacturing, and healthcare
items.why: A division of ICS (Integrated Custom Software). Horizontal ERP add-on - their own site names distribution, manufacturing, retail, and healthcare, not government; they exhibited at GFOA for public-sector ERP inventory. Founding year 1982 is from directory profiles, not their site.

items.name: Express Evaluations
items.description: Employee performance review, goal tracking, and feedback software for HR teams
items.why: General HR performance-management software - their own Solutions page segments by industry, role, and company size with no public-sector emphasis, and their /government page is 'under construction'. Third-party writeups say local government is a target segment, which is presumably why they exhibited at PSHRA. HQ not stated on site (phone is a Utah 385 area code, not enough to place them); founding year not found.

items.name: NetDocuments
items.description: Cloud document and email management with legal AI for law firms, corporate legal departments, and government legal offices
items.why: Candidate had no URL; netdocuments.com confirmed. Judgment call for the owner: it is legal-vertical rather than truly horizontal, but its primary buyers are private law firms and corporate legal, with government legal (why it exhibited at IMLA, the municipal attorneys' association) as one segment among several - so not government-primary.

items.name: TRU Solutions
items.description: Field data capture and asset inspection platform for industrial coatings, shipbuilding, pipeline, and energy construction compliance
items.why: Real product company, but their own site lists industries as coating inspection, infrastructure, marine, and oil and gas - not government. Navy shipbuilding compliance is the only public-sector-adjacent use named. Worth a look at whether this belongs in a SLED tracker at all. Founding year not found by these searches.

items.name: BLR
items.description: HR and environmental health and safety compliance software, regulatory content, and training courseware for employers in all industries
items.why: Horizontal compliance vendor - their own site claims 34,000 companies across manufacturing, construction, healthcare, and retail, with public risk pools (why they exhibited at PRIMA) as one slice. Also part publisher: revenue mixes SaaS (EHS Hero, HR Hero, TrainingToday) with attorney-verified content subscriptions, so the owner may see it as more content than product. Formerly Business & Legal Resources / M. Lee Smith Publishers.

items.name: OutSystems
items.description: Low-code and AI application development platform used to build custom apps across banking, insurance, government, manufacturing, healthcare, and retail
items.why: Horizontal dev platform - government is one of eight industries listed on their own site. Founded 2001 in Lisbon, Portugal; US headquarters now Boston.

items.name: Netskope
items.description: Cloud access security broker, SASE, and zero trust networking software for enterprises and government agencies
items.why: General-purpose enterprise cybersecurity, not government-specific. Their homepage renders almost nothing to fetch; HQ and founding year come from directory profiles rather than their own site.

items.name: Armis
items.description: Connected asset, IoT, and OT security platform for enterprises, healthcare, manufacturing, and public agencies
items.why: General cybersecurity. armis.com returns 403 to fetch and curl, so details come from directory profiles rather than page text.

items.name: Black Duck
items.description: Application security testing software - SAST, DAST, and software composition analysis - for software teams in all industries
items.why: General AppSec, not government-specific. Founding year deliberately omitted and worth a human call: the original Black Duck Software was founded in 2002, acquired by Synopsys in 2017, then sold by Synopsys to Clearlake and Francisco Partners in October 2024 and relaunched under the old name - so 2002 and 2024 are both defensible and both misleading alone.

items.name: CyberFOX
items.description: Privileged access management, password management, and DNS filtering software sold to managed service providers and lean IT teams
items.why: General cybersecurity; their own site lists MSPs first, with government and education as segments among manufacturing and enterprise. 2022 is the CyberFOX brand launch (June 2022) uniting AutoElevate, founded 2018, and Password Boss - not a clean incorporation date.

items.name: Wasabi Technologies
items.description: S3-compatible cloud object storage sold as a low-cost alternative to hyperscalers for backup, archive, AI, and video surveillance data
items.why: Horizontal cloud infrastructure - their own site names AI, healthcare, media, backup, and surveillance as target industries, not government. Founded September 2015 by David Friend and Jeff Flowers; product launched 2017.

items.name: Jamf
items.description: Apple device management and endpoint security for enterprises, schools, universities, healthcare, and small business
items.why: Candidate had no URL; jamf.com confirmed. Horizontal device management - their own site's first industry tab is Enterprise, with K-12 and Higher Education alongside. Founding year 2000 is stated on their About page (co-founded by Zach Halmstad at UW-Eau Claire); the About page names Minnesota and Wisconsin but no city, so Minneapolis is from Jamf's public company filings, not the page.

items.name: Clearspeed
items.description: Voice-analysis risk assessment used for personnel vetting, claims triage, and fraud screening across government, defense, insurance, and banking
items.why: Real product, but their own navigation splits Public Sector (government, immigration, benefits integrity, defense) from Commercial (insurance, banking, sports integrity) - it sells the same engine into many industries, so the owner should rule on scope. First major defense client was U.S. Special Operations Command in 2018. Founding year not stated on their site.

items.name: ObservSMART
items.description: Proximity-verified patient observation rounding and safety compliance software for behavioral health units, hospitals, and long-term care
items.why: Flagged rather than decided: a real product, but their own site's 500+ customers span acute care hospitals, emergency departments, skilled nursing, and long-term care - a healthcare market where public psychiatric and county facilities are one slice, not the core. Founding year not stated on the site.

items.name: Adobe
items.description: Aqua, a free digital art and drawing app for children and families, offered by Adobe alongside its wider creative software line
items.why: Not a standalone company: the site says Aqua is 'made with love by parents at Adobe' - the exhibitor is Adobe Inc. showing a consumer kids' app to public libraries. Big-tech horizontal vendor, so the owner should rule on whether it belongs at all. HQ San Jose is from general knowledge of Adobe, not the Aqua page; founding year omitted for the same reason.

items.name: CustomGuide
items.description: Editable training courseware and skill assessments for Microsoft Office, Google Workspace, compliance, and soft skills, with a built-in LMS
items.why: Candidate had no URL; customguide.com confirmed. Horizontal training content - 3,000+ organizations named include Amazon and Yale alongside government agencies, nonprofits, and public libraries. It is also more courseware than software. HQ omitted: the only locator is a 612 Minneapolis phone number, and the About and Contact pages render nothing to fetch. Founding year not found.

items.name: Answerr
items.description: AI capability assessment and AIQ credentialing platform for individuals, universities, and employers
items.why: Flagged for a human check: the candidate described 'AI voice answering for institutions', but answerr.ai today sells AI capability measurement and credentialing (legal entity Answer Labs Inc.) - either the candidate's vertical was wrong or the company pivoted, and I could not rule out a name collision. Also sells to enterprises and individuals, not just institutions. HQ and founding year not disclosed on the site.

items.description: Privileged access management and identity security software for enterprises, government agencies, and universities
items.why: General cybersecurity, not education-specific - the candidate URL was their /education landing page. beyondtrust.com returns 403 to fetch and renders nothing to curl, so HQ is from general knowledge rather than the site, and the founding year is omitted (the company is a roll-up of Symark, eEye, and the original BeyondTrust, with no single clean date).

items.name: Canva
items.description: Browser-based visual design and presentation software used by businesses, schools, universities, and nonprofits
items.why: Horizontal design tool; the candidate URL was the Canva for Campus landing page. canva.com renders nothing to curl, so HQ and founding year are from general knowledge, not the site. Legal entity Canva Pty Ltd.

items.name: Cribl
items.description: Telemetry data pipeline and observability software that routes logs, metrics, and traces for enterprise IT and security teams
items.why: Horizontal infrastructure software - roughly half the Fortune 100, with public sector one of eight industries listed. Their own Our Story timeline dates the founding by Clint Sharp, Dritan Bitincka, and Ledion Bitincka in San Francisco to July 2018.

items.name: GitLab
items.description: DevOps platform for source control, CI/CD, and security scanning used by software teams in every industry
items.why: Horizontal developer tooling. about.gitlab.com returns 403 to fetch, so HQ and founding year are from general knowledge of the public company rather than the site; GitLab is all-remote with San Francisco as its registered headquarters, so the city is nominal.

items.description: AI test automation and change-impact analysis for Oracle Cloud, Workday, and SAP ERP implementations across all industries
items.why: Horizontal ERP tooling - their own site lists eight industries with Government (SLED) as one, alongside Fortune 500 logos like Gap, Pfizer, and Dell. Their /about-us and /contact-us return 403 to curl, so HQ and founding year are not confirmed and are omitted.

items.name: Poll Everywhere
items.description: Live audience polling and response software for classroom instruction, corporate meetings, and events
items.why: Horizontal engagement tool - their own About page claims 82% of the Fortune 500 alongside 91% of R1 universities. Founded 2008 in San Francisco per that page; the company is now remote-first, so the city is nominal.

items.description: Text-to-speech and voice technology for websites, learning platforms, gaming, transportation, and embedded applications
items.why: Horizontal voice technology - their own sector menu lists gaming, transportation, workplace, government, assistive technology, healthcare, fintech, and media alongside education. HQ and founding year are not published on the site; the company operates across Europe and the US.

items.description: AI email, document, and writing productivity suite - Grammarly, Superhuman Mail, and Docs - for individuals, companies, and institutions
items.why: Horizontal productivity software; the candidate URL was the /edu landing page. Claims 40M+ daily users and 3,000+ academic institutions. HQ not published on the site.

items.name: Veeam Software
items.description: Backup, disaster recovery, and ransomware resilience software for hybrid cloud data across all industries
items.why: Horizontal data protection - their own solutions menu lists government and education alongside financial services, healthcare, enterprise, service providers, and small business. Neither their About nor Contact page states an HQ or founding year, so both are omitted.

Horizontal ESG platform sold across industry verticals (automotive, electronics, chemicals, consumer goods), not a public-sector product, despite exhibiting at NACUBO. Founding year not found by these searches.

items.description: Lease accounting and lease administration software for corporate, retail, and public-sector real estate portfolios
items.why: Horizontal lease accounting product sold across all industries; GASB 87 support is one compliance mode among ASC 842 and IFRS 16. Acquired Visual Lease, now merged into this brand. Part of CoStar Group. Founding year not found by these searches.

items.name: FinQuery
items.description: Lease, debt, and accrual accounting automation software for finance teams in any industry
items.why: Formerly LeaseQuery. Horizontal accounting-compliance product; government issuers are one segment among corporates and CPA firms.

items.description: Accounting, payroll, and ERP software for small and mid-sized businesses across all industries
items.why: sage.com blocks automated fetch (Cloudflare 403) for both WebFetch and curl; details from company profile sources. Horizontal SMB accounting/ERP vendor with a public sector practice (Sage Intacct), not a govtech-specific product.

items.name: Oracle
items.description: Cloud infrastructure, database, ERP, and HCM software sold to enterprises and governments across every industry
items.why: Candidate was listed as the US operating entity Oracle America, Inc.; the canonical brand is Oracle (Oracle Corporation). Horizontal big-tech vendor with a public sector division, not a govtech-specific company.

items.name: Checkbox
items.description: No-code legal request intake, matter management, and workflow automation software for in-house legal teams
items.why: No URL was supplied; resolved to checkbox.ai (Checkbox Technology Pty Ltd), not the unrelated Checkbox survey software at checkbox.com. Horizontal legal-ops product whose named customers are corporates (BMW, PepsiCo, SAP, Deloitte); municipal law departments are one buyer type among many.

items.name: Multi-Health Systems Inc. (MHS)
items.description: Psychological and risk-needs assessments delivered through an online assessment platform, sold to clinical, education, public safety, and corporate talent buyers
items.why: Judgment call: MHS is an assessment publisher rather than a pure software company, and it sells across clinical, education, corrections, and corporate HR. Its offender risk-needs instruments (LS/CMI, YLS/CMI) are the reason it exhibits at APPA, but the business is not government-specific.

items.name: Vexcel
items.description: Aerial imagery, 3D models, and AI-derived property data licensed to government, insurance, utilities, telecom, energy, and financial services
items.why: Given URL vexcelgroup.com did not respond; the live commercial site is vexceldata.com (footer entity Vexcel Imaging US, Inc.). Horizontal geospatial data business: government property assessment is one of eight named industries alongside insurance, which is the largest commercial segment. Founded 1992 in Graz, Austria as Vexcel Imaging; US group HQ now Boulder, CO.

items.name: KYND
items.description: Cyber risk scanning and portfolio monitoring software sold to insurance brokers, underwriters, financial services firms, and risk pools
items.why: General-purpose cyber risk analytics distributed mainly through the insurance channel; public entity risk pools are one buyer segment among brokers, carriers, and corporates. Backed by Verisk and BGF. HQ and founding year from funding press, not the company site.

items.name: Siteimprove
items.description: Web accessibility, content quality, analytics, and SEO software for organizations in government, higher education, healthcare, finance, and retail
items.why: Horizontal digital-presence platform; government and higher ed are two of many named verticals, with corporates such as Vodafone, BT, and Costco as flagship customers. Legal entity Siteimprove A/S.

items.name: Microsoft
items.description: Cloud infrastructure, productivity, and AI software sold to enterprises, governments, and consumers worldwide
items.why: Big-tech horizontal vendor with a public sector division; not govtech-specific.

items.name: Ping Identity
items.description: Identity and access management, verification, and fraud protection software for large enterprises
items.why: General-purpose IAM: the company markets itself on Fortune 100 and large-bank adoption, with government as one vertical. Denver HQ confirmed on the company's contact page; founding year is from general reference sources, not the site. Owned by Thoma Bravo.

items.name: CoreView
items.description: Microsoft 365 tenant governance, configuration management, and license optimization software for enterprise IT teams
items.why: Horizontal Microsoft 365 management tool; named customers span higher ed, state government, banking, shipping, and nonprofits. Company lists a US HQ in Washington, DC, an EMEA HQ in Milan, Italy, and an Australian office. GovRAMP Premier Member. Founding year not found by these searches.

items.name: Cloudera
items.description: Hybrid data lakehouse and enterprise AI platform sold to large organizations across all industries
items.why: General enterprise data platform (Global 2000 positioning) with public sector as one vertical. HQ and founding year could not be confirmed on cloudera.com itself; both come from general reference sources and should be spot-checked.

items.name: Nomic Networks
items.description: Managed network detection and response and managed security operations for organizations with small IT teams
items.why: Formerly Sentinel IPS. Delivered largely as a managed service rather than self-serve software, and sold across local government, banking, healthcare, and higher ed, so it is horizontal cybersecurity rather than a govtech product. HQ and founding year from Crunchbase/ZoomInfo-style profiles.

items.name: Zoom Communications
items.description: Video meetings, phone, chat, and contact center software sold to businesses, schools, and governments
items.why: Renamed from Zoom Video Communications to Zoom Communications, Inc. in 2024. Horizontal communications platform; education and government are two of many named verticals.

items.name: Logikcull
items.description: Cloud e-discovery, legal hold, and public records request automation for law firms, corporations, government agencies, and schools
items.why: Acquired by Reveal Data in August 2023 and now operates as a Reveal brand; the logikcull.com site is still live with its own product pages. Horizontal legal tech, with FOIA and public records handling as one workflow among corporate e-discovery use cases.

items.name: ScreenSteps
items.description: Knowledge base, SOP authoring, and in-app agent guidance software for contact centers and regulated back offices
items.why: Horizontal knowledge-operations tool; the industries it names are credit unions, banks, farm credit associations, contact centers, and law firms, with human services agencies as an adjacent buyer. Founding year not found by these searches.

items.name: PaymentVision
items.description: Payment gateway for card, ACH, and check payments taken by phone, web, and API, sold to lenders, collectors, healthcare billers, utilities, and government agencies
items.why: A brand of Autoscribe Corporation. Horizontal biller-facing payments processor; housing authorities and municipalities are one of five named verticals alongside collections and consumer finance.

items.name: Amigo AI
items.description: Platform for building and deploying AI clinical agents that automate patient-facing workflows for healthcare providers
items.why: Judgment call worth a second look: the buyers are clinics and health systems across primary care, orthopedics, women's health, oncology, and behavioral health, so it is a healthcare AI vendor rather than a public-agency product, despite exhibiting at NatCon. HQ and founding year are not published on the site and were not found by these searches.

items.name: Kipu Health
items.description: CRM, EMR, billing, and compliance platform for addiction treatment, eating disorder, and behavioral health facilities
items.why: Judgment call worth a second look: a real behavioral health software product, but its named market is private residential and outpatient treatment centers rather than county or state agencies, so it may not belong on a public-sector tracker. Founding year not found by these searches.

items.name: Oracle Health
items.description: Electronic health record and clinical data platform for hospitals, health systems, and behavioral health providers
items.why: This is Oracle's healthcare division, the former Cerner, acquired by Oracle in 2022 and still operating from the Kansas City area campus. It is the same corporate entity as the separate Oracle candidate from PSHRA 2026, so the two should probably be merged rather than carded twice. Founding year omitted because Oracle (1977), Cerner (1979), and Oracle Health (2022) are three different dates.

items.name: Candid
items.description: Database of roughly 1.9 million US nonprofits plus grants and funder data, licensed to nonprofits, grantmakers, and public libraries
items.why: Candid is itself a 501(c)(3) nonprofit (EIN 13-1837418) formed in 2019 by the merger of GuideStar and Foundation Center, so 2019 is the merged entity's date, not the lineage's. Its primary users are nonprofits and funders; public libraries are one distribution channel, which is why this is flagged rather than carded as govtech. HQ from general reference sources; the site's contact page did not resolve.

items.name: Data Axle
items.description: US business and consumer reference databases, sold to marketers broadly and to libraries and academic institutions as Reference Solutions
items.why: Reference Solutions is the library-facing product line of a general-purpose B2B and consumer data company (formerly Infogroup), which is why this is scope review rather than govtech. Corporate locations listed are Grapevine TX, Boston MA, and Omaha NE, with Grapevine listed first; the site says 'since 1972' rather than naming a founding year outright.

items.name: SenSource, Inc.
items.description: Stereo-video people counting sensors and occupancy analytics software for retail, libraries, museums, campuses, and public buildings
items.why: Horizontal traffic-analytics vendor: retail is listed first among ten industries, and the offering is a sensor-plus-software package with installation services, so it is part hardware business.

items.description: Cloud patch management and endpoint vulnerability remediation software for IT teams across industries
items.why: Could not read the site: action1.com serves a Cloudflare JavaScript challenge to WebFetch and to curl with full browser headers, and the session's web search budget was exhausted before an alternate source could be checked. Verdict, description, and category rest on general knowledge of Action1 as a horizontal patch management vendor and should be verified by hand; HQ and founding year are deliberately omitted rather than guessed.

items.name: Carousel Digital Signage
items.description: Cloud digital signage content management and emergency messaging software for schools, campuses, offices, hospitals, and government buildings
items.why: A product of Tightrope Media Systems. Horizontal signage platform sold across five named industries. The site claims nearly 30 years in business but never states a founding year, so none is recorded.

items.name: Commvault
items.description: Data backup, cyber recovery, and identity resilience software for enterprises across all industries
items.why: Horizontal enterprise data protection vendor; government, healthcare, financial services, and education are named as verticals. Publicly traded (NASDAQ: CVLT). HQ and founding year from general reference sources, not the site.

items.description: Event registration, venue sourcing, mobile app, and check-in software for event and marketing teams across all industries
items.why: Horizontal event management platform with a higher-ed page; the company markets on 89% of the Fortune 100 as customers. Legal name Cvent, Inc. Address from the site footer; founding year from general reference sources, matching the site's '25+ years' claim. Sector assignment is awkward: the product is event software, so it was mapped to Events & Tourism rather than to the conference it exhibited at.

items.description: DNS, DHCP, and IP address management software with DNS security, sold to enterprises and service providers across all industries
items.why: Horizontal network infrastructure vendor; reference customers are Netflix, Heineken, Orange, Airbus, and Credit Agricole, with education one of six named verticals. Originally a French company (EfficientIP SAS); West Chester, PA is the address listed first on its contact page and appears to be the US HQ, so the corporate HQ in France is worth confirming. Founding year from the site's 'Since 2004'.

items.description: Salesforce-native scheduling, booking, and resource reservation software sold across education, healthcare, hospitality, retail, and financial services
items.why: Horizontal Salesforce ISV listing ten industries; education is one. Founding year not found by these searches.

items.description: IT service management, enterprise service management, and CRM software sold across public sector, retail, education, healthcare, and financial services
items.why: Corporate entity is Halo Service Solutions; HaloITSM is one product alongside HaloPSA, HaloCRM, and HaloCSM. Horizontal service-desk vendor across roughly fifteen named industries. Founding year not found by these searches.

items.name: MyWorkDrive
items.description: VPN-free secure remote access to on-premises and cloud file servers, sold across healthcare, education, government, legal, finance, and manufacturing
items.why: Legal entity MyWorkDrive, LLC. Horizontal file-access product spanning seven named industries. HQ and founding year not published on the site and not found by these searches.

items.name: Orchestry
items.description: Microsoft 365 workspace provisioning, lifecycle, and governance software for IT teams across construction, healthcare, higher education, legal, manufacturing, and public sector
items.why: Legal entity Orchestry Software Inc. Horizontal Microsoft ecosystem ISV; overlaps directly with the CoreView candidate from NASCIO 2026. HQ and founding year not published on the site and not found by these searches.

items.name: Red Hat
items.description: Enterprise Linux, Kubernetes, automation, and AI platform subscriptions sold to large organizations in every industry
items.why: An IBM subsidiary since 2019. Horizontal enterprise open source vendor with an academic program; not govtech-specific.

items.why: Three named markets: technical hiring, higher education and certification proctoring, and assessment platforms, so corporate recruiting is co-equal with education. items.description: Work and project portfolio management platform sold to enterprises across every industry
items.why: Horizontal work management vendor marketing on 85%+ Fortune 500 adoption; government and higher education are two of six named verticals. Legal name Smartsheet Inc. HQ and founding year from general reference sources because the site does not publish either.

items.why: Horizontal asset-tracking vendor (Ingenium cloud and AssetWIN on-prem) with a mixed software-plus-services model; public sector is one named market among many, alongside Fortune 500 clients

items.why: Horizontal HR/risk workflow product - government is one of roughly fifteen industries listed alongside manufacturing, retail, and hospitality. items.why: Horizontal verification data network - government benefits is one of six named markets alongside mortgage, personal lending, background checks, tenant screening, and gig economy.
